drafts.after: The falling away and the man of sin come before the Day of the Lord. First principle: the end follows an order. The falling away comes first, and then the lawless one is revealed. Daniel 7's little power and Jesus' warnings about deception meet here.
drafts.reason: 'The apostasy and the man of sin precede the Day' is said as the falling away and the man of sin coming before the Day of the Lord; 'the end has asequence' is corrected to 'the end follows an order' (the source had a missing space); and the semicolon-joined second half is split so the order and the two witnesses each stand alone. Claims kept: falling away and man of sin come before the Day; falling away first, lawless one revealed; Daniel 7's little power and Jesus' deception warnings converge.

drafts.after: The lawless one comes with counterfeit power, signs, and lying wonders. First principle: he makes a copy of Pentecost. He shows power and signs, but he has no truth. Jesus warned that great signs would deceive even the elect.
drafts.reason: 'photocopies Pentecost' becomes 'makes a copy of Pentecost'; the semicolon that joined two ideas becomes a sentence break; and 'power and signs without truth' is written out with a subject and a verb. Claims kept: counterfeit power, signs, and lying wonders; the lawless one copies Pentecost; power and signs without truth; Jesus warned that great signs deceive even the elect.

drafts.after: The man of sin puts himself on display in the temple and claims to be God. First principle: Daniel 11's exalting king and Ezekiel's prince-tyrant are the family line of this seated blasphemy. The abomination takes a chair.
drafts.reason: 'The self-deifying exhibition in the temple' becomes the man of sin putting himself on display and claiming to be God, which is what the verse says; 'are the lineage of' becomes 'are the family line of'; and the em-dash sentence yields the closing claim its own sentence. Claims kept: self-deifying display in the temple; Daniel 11's king and Ezekiel's prince-tyrant are its lineage; the abomination takes a chair.

drafts.after: The Wicked is revealed, and the breath of His coming destroys him. First principle: Isaiah 11's slaying by the breath of his lips is how the anti-christ meets his end. A word kills the warrior.
drafts.reason: the em-dash clause becomes a comma-and clause with the verb made active, so 'the breath of His coming' is carried as it stands; 'the mechanism of the anti-christ's end' becomes 'how the anti-christ meets his end'; and 'breath-of-lips slaying' is written out. Claims kept: the Wicked is revealed; the breath of His coming destroys him; Isaiah 11's breath-of-lips slaying is the mechanism; a word kills the warrior.

drafts.after: God sends a lie as judgment on those who refused the truth. First principle: the delusion is itself the sentence. When a person resists the truth, a lie he believes becomes God's judgment on him. Ahab's lying spirit was the earlier picture of this.
drafts.reason: 'The judicial lie' names God as the one who sends it; 'delusion is judgment' becomes 'the delusion is itself the sentence'; the passive 'when truth is resisted' becomes 'when a person resists the truth'; and 'prefigured' carries the frozen glossary rendering for a type, 'the earlier picture'. Claims kept: the lie is judgment on those who refused the truth; a believed lie becomes God's sentence; Ahab's lying spirit prefigured it.

drafts.after: This is the day when Christ is admired in those who believe. First principle: at the coming, Christ's glory is displayed in the saints he has glorified. The testimony they believed becomes visible admiration.
drafts.reason: the compressed coinage 'The admired-in-believers day' is written out with its actor; 'displayed in the saints He glorified' stays and its subject is named as Christ's glory at the coming; and the final claim is kept in plain order. Claims kept: the day when Christ is admired in believers; his glory is displayed in the saints he glorified; the believed testimony becomes visible admiration.

drafts.after: Paul writes the greeting with his own hand, and that proves the letter is genuine. First principle: forged letters were a real danger in that age. Proof of the letter's authenticity came down to a person. The apostle's signature was the church's security feature.
drafts.reason: 'The handwritten token authenticates every epistle' becomes the greeting written by Paul's own hand proving the letter genuine; 'in an age of forged letters' becomes forged letters being a real danger then; and 'authenticity is personal' becomes proof coming down to a person. Claims kept: the handwritten greeting authenticates the letter; forged letters were the danger; authenticity is personal; the apostle's signature is the church's security feature.

drafts.after: God establishes you and keeps you from evil, and he does it because he is faithful. First principle: a believer's stability does not come from himself. The Faithful One makes him stand and guards him against the evil one.
drafts.reason: 'Establishment and keeping from evil rest on His faithfulness' gains the actor and a verb; 'the believer's stability is not self-generated' becomes 'does not come from himself'; and the closing clause names the Faithful One who makes him stand and guards him. Claims kept: establishment and keeping rest on His faithfulness; stability is not self-generated; the Faithful One establishes and guards against the evil one.

drafts.after: When the Lord is revealed, he brings fiery vengeance on those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel. First principle: the sword from the mouth in Isaiah 11 and the flaming judgment belong to the same returning Lord who saved.
drafts.reason: 'Revelation includes fiery vengeance' is stated as what happens when the Lord is revealed, and 'the ignorant and the disobedient' is spelled out as those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel, which is the wording of the verse; 'the Isaiah 11 mouth-sword' becomes 'the sword from the mouth in Isaiah 11'. Claims kept: fiery vengeance at the revealing; on the ignorant and disobedient; the Isaiah 11 mouth-sword and the flaming judgment belong to the same returning Lord who saved.

drafts.after: Believers who are troubled receive rest when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven. First principle: the rest is timed to that revealing. Relief for the troubled arrives with the display of mighty angels.
drafts.reason: 'Tribulated believers' becomes believers who are troubled; 'the revealed-from-heaven appearing' becomes the Lord Jesus being revealed from heaven; 'rest is timed to revelation' is split off as its own sentence; and 'the mighty-angel display' becomes the display of mighty angels. Claims kept: troubled believers receive rest; rest is timed to the revealing; relief comes with the mighty angels.
